guarantees.claim: For i=0..5, the output b_buf[i] is driven to equal the input b[i] through the prim_buf primitive.

assumptions.claim: The b[i] signals must be glitch-free; any glitch would propagate to b_buf[i] and may leak mask-share information in the masked S-box computation.
assumptions.risk: Side-channel leakage of secret share through transitions on b_buf[i], breaking the masking countermeasure.

assumptions.claim: The prim_buf cells must exhibit uniform propagation delay across all bits of each 4-bit slice; any skew could create transient glitches on b_buf[i].
assumptions.risk: Unequal delay among bits of a mask share may cause observable glitches, undermining the noise-free assumption needed for masking security.

assumptions.claim: Unconnected ports of prim_buf (e.g., enable, clear) must default to active-enable and inactive-clear so that the buffer always passes in_i to out_i.
assumptions.cond: when the instance lacks explicit connections to optional ports
assumptions.risk: If the primitive defaults to disabled or cleared state, b_buf[i] may become undefined or stuck, corrupting the masked data path.

uncertain_points.claim: The declarations of b and b_buf are not visible; each element must be exactly 4 bits wide to match the Width parameter of prim_buf. A width mismatch could cause truncation or compilation error.
uncertain_points.cond: when the surrounding module defines b and b_buf
uncertain_points.risk: If b[i] is wider than 4 bits, the buffer truncates, possibly discarding mask material and weakening security.

uncertain_points.claim: The purpose of gen_b_buf (buffering b into b_buf) is undocumented. It may be intended for glitch resistance or timing; if it is insufficient, masked S‑box operations could still leak.
uncertain_points.cond: when the target technology or attack scenario is considered
uncertain_points.risk: An incomplete or ineffective buffer may not prevent side-channel leakage, compromising the AES mask.
